prompt: A desktop draft editor was changed so closing a dirty document presents Save, Discard, and Cancel outcomes. Run the acceptance test through the supported application boundary. Saving must persist the exact edited Unicode content and reopen it after a fresh process start; Discard must close without changing the last persisted revision; Cancel must leave the editor open and dirty; and an injected save rejection must leave the document open with the prior persisted revision intact and expose the documented error state. Reopen the document after each state-changing branch and report each acceptance claim separately.

requirements: the starting document has persisted revision 4 with known baseline text
the fixture can inject one deterministic save rejection without changing storage
the supported app harness can choose Save, Discard, or Cancel and can restart the process between branches
persisted revision and content can be inspected independently from the editor view

falsifiableChecks.assertion: Save persists edited Unicode content, Discard preserves the prior persisted revision, and Cancel leaves the dirty editor open without persisting.
Injected save rejection leaves the document open, surfaces the documented error, and leaves independent persisted state unchanged.
Fresh-process reopen after every state-changing branch matches the independently observed persisted revision and content.

evidence: branch coverage maps to distinct user-visible state transitions
persistence is verified independently from the live editor
failure evidence is not upgraded into a broader reliability claim

requiredEvidence: explicit unavailable or simulated evidence labels
